newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., approves Heat arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., approves Heat arena deal.

text.p: Florida's Dade County Commission has approved a 30-year lease with the Miami Heat, allowing the basketball team to build a privately financed arena on public waterfront land adjacent to Port of Miami.

The deal was approved late Thursday in a 9-2 vote. It calls for the county to pay $6.5 million a year for 30 years for arena operating costs, using revenues from the county's six percent tax on hotel rooms.
The county also agreed to pay the Heat $2 million a year for control of naming rights at the 20,000-seat arena. The county would keep any naming rights revenues in excess of $2 million.
In exchange, the basketball team will pay $500,000 a year to support Dade County parks, and give the county 40 percent of any profits over $14 million a year.

The county originally planned to issue tax-exempt bonds to build the arena but opponents forced a referendum on the plan and the Heat agreed to private financing when polls suggested the referendum could fail.
The team now plans to sell privately placed bonds via Prudential Securities Inc to build the $228 million arena.

The county is still negotiating to buy or lease the 59-acre site from the City of Miami, using Port of Miami revenues. Once the land is sold, the Heat arena would cover eight acres and the rest would be used to build a new cruise ship terminal, shops and a maritime park.

The agreement to use the bed tax money to pay arena operating costs angered supporters of the county's planned $169 million performing arts center, which is to be built with bonds backed by the bed tax.

The county anticipates there will be enough bed tax revenue for both projects, but the deal makes it unlikely the arts center will receive the surplus revenues supporters had hoped for to buy equipment and fund improvements such as a pedestrian bridge over busy Biscayne Boulevard. The arts center site is just north of the arena site.
